question: Should Reef permanently own and support the Kubernetes/PostgreSQL relay adapter, Helm chart, database migrations, and parity contract alongside the Cloudflare relay?
rationale: The implementation creates a durable second production platform and operational compatibility commitment; code quality and tests cannot determine whether maintainers want to own that support surface.

options.title: Sponsor the second adapter
options.body: Accept Kubernetes/PostgreSQL as a supported Reef platform after the security finding and proof gate are resolved.

options.title: Externalize deployment ownership
options.body: Keep only the generic relay-core seam in Reef and move the Node/PostgreSQL adapter and Helm chart to a separately owned repository or package.

options.title: Decline platform expansion
options.body: Retain Cloudflare as the only supported relay implementation and close the PR without adopting the new operational surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the second adapter
recommendation.body: Accept Kubernetes/PostgreSQL as a supported Reef platform after the security finding and proof gate are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The design document identifies Peter as the approver of the current Reef architecture, so he is the best available owner for expanding that boundary.
